correctness.rationale: The singleton valuation argument gives \(\mathsf{Alex}\) iff \(q_f\) increasing for every finite chain, with all quantifiers made explicit; \(q_f\) is regressive/idempotent and hence the floor retraction onto ordered fixed roots. Nonroot arcs stay in their fiber, reach their root, and uniquely form a directed tree, while roots have \(n-s\) independent legal outgoing successors. The reverse construction proves \(q_f\) monotone. Cayley multiplication and composition sum count each map exactly once; boundary n=1 checked. A standalone independently evaluated semantics checker verifies all maps/valuations through n=5, tree criterion through n=7 and recurrence to n=10; finite checks are supplemental, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 modal-temporal closure/eventuality law motivates the exact question of what remains when continuity is dropped. A natural canonical structural classification and a full infinite-family exact enumeration with computable recurrence answer that question, not a narrow arbitrary fixed case. At n=5 the noncontinuity extension is substantial (1825 axiom-valid functions vs 126 order-preserving functions). It yields semantic test families and isolates the true orbit-confluence constraint without falsely claiming results about global axiomatizability.
